title: Power Apps: row summaries in model-driven apps reach GCC and GCC High
summary: The roadmap details, configuration paths and licensing statements are supported. Two minor corrections remain: describe availability as planned rather than firm, and acknowledge that the configuration guide and FAQ describe different scopes for maker configuration.

claims.claim: The roadmap status is In development.

claims.fix: Replace the summary with: "Microsoft plans AI-generated row summaries for model-driven apps in GCC and GCC High, targeting November CY2026 in the weekly release channel from version 2611.1." Replace "The roadmap lists general availability for November CY2026" with "The roadmap targets general availability for November CY2026".

claims.claim: Row summaries provide an AI-generated overview of a record in a model-driven app.
claims.quote: Row summaries are AI-generated summaries of a record's data shown on a form in a model-driven app.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes expanding the experience already available to commercial customers to government environments.
claims.quote: This release brings the row summary experience available to commercial customers to supported government environments

claims.claim: The roadmap says the expansion meets applicable compliance and data-boundary requirements.
claims.quote: while meeting their applicable compliance and data-boundary requirements.

claims.claim: Admins and makers enable and configure the capability for model-driven app users.
claims.quote: Admins and makers enable and configure row summaries for users in their model-driven apps.

claims.claim: Summaries appear in the Insights bar on main forms.
claims.quote: From the Insights bar at the top of main forms.

claims.claim: Users access summaries through the Summary action on view pages.
claims.quote: From view pages by selecting the inline Summary action in the grid, which opens the summary for a record in a modal popup.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls prose
claims.claim: Makers specify the columns included in a table's summary through a custom prompt.
claims.quote: Write a custom prompt to specify which columns should be included in a Copilot-generated row summary.

claims.claim: Microsoft's Power Platform Copilot FAQ says Copilot adheres to existing data permissions and policies.
claims.quote: Copilot adheres to existing data permissions and policies

claims.claim: The Copilot FAQ says responses are based only on data the user personally can access.
claims.quote: its responses to you're based only on data that you personally can access.

claims.claim: Learn documents a column-security limitation for form fill assistance.
claims.quote: Fields that have column security aren't currently supported.

claims.claim: The row-summary guidance does not document the form fill assistance column-security limitation for row summaries.
claims.quote: Searched: "row summaries" "column security"; Power Apps row summary usage analytics report column security secured columns. Opened record-summaries, configure-form-row-summary, faq-record-summaries and form-filling-assistance; no matching row-summary limitation.

claims.claim: The feature reads data from the current record.
claims.quote: The feature reads the data on the current record

claims.claim: The feature generates a natural-language summary.
claims.quote: generates a short, natural-language summary that highlights key information

claims.claim: Generated summaries may be wrong.
claims.quote: The response generated might be incorrect or misleading and could cause unintended outcomes from the flow or app.

claims.claim: The feature is hidden from users who lack the required licence.

claims.claim: Usage may be subject to service limits.

claims.claim: Government-specific pricing for this row-summary rollout is not yet published.
claims.quote: Searched: "row summaries" "government" pricing; "row summaries" "GCC High" pricing AI Builder. Opened record-summaries, administer-licensing and powerapps-us-government; no government-specific row-summary price found.

claims.claim: Government licensing terms may differ from the general product guidance.
claims.quote: You can access Power Apps US Government plans through the following offerings. Each plan is offered as a monthly subscription

claims.claim: The default state for this government rollout is not stated, with differing general Learn descriptions reported in the body.
claims.quote: Searched: "row summaries" "GCC" default setting. Read roadmap, powerapps-us-government, record-summaries and faq-record-summaries; no government rollout default. General guidance says administrator must enable; FAQ says environment setting is on by default and makers must configure prompts.

claims.claim: The row summaries page says a Power Platform administrator must enable Row summaries for the environment.
claims.quote: A Power Platform administrator must enable Row summaries for the environment in the Power Platform admin center under Copilot > Settings > Power Apps > Summary.

claims.claim: The FAQ says the AI insight cards environment setting enabling row summaries is on by default.
claims.quote: The AI insight cards environment setting that enables row summaries is on by default.

claims.claim: The FAQ says makers still need to configure and turn on summary prompts on individual tables.
claims.quote: Makers still need to configure and turn on summary prompts on individual tables so that row summaries appear on the corresponding forms and views.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: The environment control is in Power Platform admin center > Copilot > Settings > Power Apps > Summary > Row summaries > environment > Edit setting.
claims.quote: In the navigation pane, select Copilot, and then select Settings. Under Power Apps, locate Row summaries in the Summary section. Select the environment, and then select Edit setting.

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls table and prose
claims.claim: An equivalent automation call for the row-summary environment control is not documented in the guidance.
claims.quote: Searched: row summaries AI insight cards environment setting Power Platform API pac admin PowerShell automation; EnableFormInsights. Opened row-summary guidance, SDK property and Update Environment Management Settings reference; no versioned operation documents the deciding row-summary property.

claims.claim: The maker control is in Power Apps > Tables > table > Customizations > Row summary.
claims.quote: Sign in to Power Apps (make.powerapps.com) select Tables on the left navigation pane, and then open the table where you want to configure a row summary. Under Customizations, select Row summary.

claims.claim: An equivalent automation operation for configuring the summary prompt and its visibility is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: row summary AI Skill Config table entity reference prompt Show row summary API; "AI Skill Config" "entity reference"; "aiskillconfig" Web API. Opened configure-form-row-summary and ai-skill-config-table; no operation and deciding properties for this control found.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Governance controls table and prose
claims.claim: The maker configuration applies to all main forms and views for the table.
claims.quote: When you configure the row summary, it applies to all views and main forms for the table.
claims.fix: After the table-wide scope statement, add: "The configuration guide describes table-wide scope; the row-summary FAQ instead describes configuring and hiding summaries on specific forms (https://learn.microsoft.com/power-apps/maker/common/faq-record-summaries)."

claims.where: controls[1].note; Governance controls table and prose
claims.claim: Show row summary hides custom summaries configured through the row-summary experience.
claims.quote: The Show row summary toggle affects only custom row summaries configured from this row summary experience.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Governance controls table and prose
claims.claim: Show row summary does not hide Microsoft-provided summaries or summaries configured through other applications, which have their own controls.
claims.quote: It doesn't hide summaries provided by Microsoft or summaries configured through another application or experience, such as Customer Service summaries for custom tables.

claims.claim: A separate tenant switch specific to GCC and GCC High is not documented on either the UI or automation surface.
claims.quote: Searched: "row summaries" "government" "switch"; row summaries GCC GCC High tenant switch default government pricing. Opened powerapps-us-government, record-summaries, configure-form-row-summary and copilot-hub; no separate cloud-specific tenant switch found.

claims.claim: The documented row-summary availability control is an environment setting rather than a separate government-cloud setting.
claims.quote: A Power Platform administrator must enable Row summaries for the environment

claims.claim: The Copilot settings experience is the primary environment-level availability control for row summaries.
claims.quote: Use the Copilot settings experience in the Power Platform admin center as the primary environment-level control for row summaries:

claims.claim: The control over who can use AI features in model-driven apps is in preview.
claims.quote: This capability is currently in preview

claims.claim: The user allow/exclude control is only for environments activated for Managed Environments.
claims.quote: is only for environments activated for managed environments, with a subset of Copilot features adhering to it.

claims.claim: The preview user control lets admins explicitly allow specific users.
claims.quote: Admins can define who within an environment can use Copilot capabilities in model-driven apps—either by explicitly allowing specific users

claims.claim: The preview user control also lets admins allow all users except a defined exclusion list.
claims.quote: or allowing all users except a defined exclusion list.

claims.claim: Power Apps Row summary is listed among the capabilities adhering to the user allow/exclude control.
claims.quote: Review the following table to learn which capabilities adhere to this configuration. ... Power Apps | Row summary

claims.claim: The Copilot hub page does not say whether its preview user allow/exclude control is available in GCC or GCC High.
claims.quote: Searched: row summaries GCC GCC High tenant switch default government pricing; "row summaries" "GCC" default setting. Opened copilot-hub in full and powerapps-us-government; copilot-hub states no government-cloud availability for this preview control.

claims.claim: The older AI insight cards settings location currently exposes the same control.
claims.quote: The same control is currently also available as AI insight cards in the environment feature settings.

claims.claim: The AI insight cards settings location will be removed in a future release.
claims.quote: The AI insight cards location will be removed in a future release.

claims.claim: A row-summary-specific usage report is not documented as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: "row summaries" "usage" "report"; Power Apps row summary usage analytics report column security secured columns. Opened copilot-hub, record-summaries and faq-record-summaries; hub documents data entry and exploration analytics, not a row-summary-specific report.

claims.claim: The licensing model is mixed, combining the stated user-licence requirements with AI Builder consumption.
claims.quote: AI Builder is licensed on a capacity basis. Building custom and testing models (including prompts) doesn't require AI Builder credits or Copilot Credits. Running them in agents, agent flows, apps, or flows consume these credits.

claims.claim: The variable cost rating reflects consumption of AI Builder credits or Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: In Power Apps and Power Automate, AI Builder features consume either AI Builder credits (Licensing and AI Builder credits), or Copilot Credits (Licensing and Copilot Credits).

claims.claim: Summary prompts process grounding data through a generative AI service.
claims.quote: Prompt builder prompts run on Azure OpenAI Service hosted by Microsoft. ... Customer prompts (input) with its grounding data and the model responses (output) aren't used to train or improve Azure OpenAI Service foundation models.

claims.claim: The environment setting controls row summaries on both model-driven app main forms and view pages.
claims.quote: This setting controls row summaries on both model-driven app main forms and view pages.
